column5: ## Building an Enduring Foundation

column4: I have always had a fascination with questions. Why is *something* true? What made it that way? How do we know? How are we sure? If *something* is true, what else is true? What is false? This fascination goes beyond a desire to be correct on a surface level, but to know deeply and precisely, and to be able to clearly articulate the new gained understanding.
column5: I have long been captivated by questions. Why is *something* true? What made it so? How do we know? How can we be certain? If *something* is true, what else is true? What is false? This captivation goes beyond a desire to be superficially right; it moves toward knowing deeply and precisely, and being able to articulate newly gained understanding clearly.

column4: While communication is common, effective and precise communication is challenging. To effectively communicate a message the author and originator must have an idea. However, the idea alone like water on a hard surface-its edges and boundaries are poorly defined, fluid, and easily moved around.
column5: Communication is common, but effective and accurate communication is difficult. To convey a message effectively, the originator and author must have an idea. Yet that idea by itself is like water on a hard surface—its contours and boundaries are indistinct, fluid, and easily stirred up.

column4: We use words, terms, and phrases to transform the raw idea from vaguely shaped to precisely shaped. Words give our idea a boundary, they help us distinguish and separate between what the idea is, and what it is not. Now our shaped idea must be transmitted and received through some medium. Whether in long form text, like this book, or short form text, like a social media post, or in oral form, like a conversation or a video recording, the medium transmits the now well-formed idea to the recipient.
column5: We use words, terms, and turns of phrase to transform raw ideas from a vague form into a precise one. Words give ideas boundaries and help distinguish and separate what the idea is and what it is not. Our shaped ideas must be transmitted and received through some medium. Whether in long form like this book, in short form like a social media post, or in spoken form like a conversation or video, the medium conveys well-formed ideas to the recipient.

column4: Every great human work is the by-product of effective communication. One man’s labor can only accomplish so much. To really build or perform something great, many men (speaking here generically of mankind) must labor together in a shared purpose, with a shared idea. Barring naturally occurring disasters (like a volcanic eruption) we also know that the greatest calamities to ever occur usually did so in significant part because of missing, broken or distorted communication. Truly life and death are in the power of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21).
column5: Every great human achievement is a byproduct of effective communication. There is only so much that can be accomplished by the labor of a single person. To build and carry out something truly great, many people (here I mean humanity in general) must work together under a common purpose and common ideas. Except for spontaneous natural disasters (such as volcanic eruptions), we also know that many of the greatest calamities that have ever occurred arose in large part because communication was missing, broken, or distorted. Truly, life and death are in the power of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21).

column4: What we believe and how we communicate it has the power to build a person, a family, a community, a nation, or has the power to equally destroy them. Because belief is expressed through action and communication, it defines the role we play in existence. Our beliefs shape not just our lives, but to a degree the lives of everyone around us.
